_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002).

tasks.title: Batch feature_build live-world reads (prefetch before hot loops)
tasks.notes: Found in bake-off R-014: feature_build dry-run took 40+ min because surf/top_solid/floor_y (feature_build.py ~601/624/854/868), the leaves filter (~1393) and clearing columns (~752/756) read one block per block_scan_region call, and mc_paced.Paced(1.1s) throttles each (server answers <10ms). Fix: call self.live.prefetch(positions) (World.prefetch, site_kit ~426, uses read_many) per feature before each hot loop; leave the block() loops alone so results are identical by construction. Guard with getattr(self.live,'prefetch',None) for fakes; overlay must not prefetch cells served from .cells; prefetch inside plan construction (StaleRead after mark_written). Test: counting fake MCP via LiveBlocks(mcp=fake,...) asserting identical plan vs per-block path and an upper bound on scan calls. Measure one 65k-volume scan latency before claiming seconds. Then record commit hash + 'speed only, outputs identical' in R-014 notes.

tasks.title: Sweep other scripts for per-block live-read loops
tasks.notes: After the feature_build fix, audit .block( loops in geo, plant_cell_canopy, site_recover, site_walk, entrances, cell_marker, mask_undo, osm_footprints. Fix only real hot loops by prefetch. Audit first.

tasks.title: Warn when LiveBlocks issues many tiny scans
tasks.notes: Count block_scan_region calls in LiveBlocks; warn on stderr past N tiny scans per store lifetime. Never raise (a hard failure mid-apply is worse than slow). Optional: drop if the test-level scan-call bound in the batching task is enough. Possible later ticket: shorter Paced interval for read-only scans.

tasks.title: Bake-off world has no OSM vector_map; feature_build read another world's data
tasks.notes: R-014 designer dry-run passed osm_root=../southampton-build/reference/vector_map because worlds/bakeoff lacks it, a cross-world read despite 'never touch southampton-build' (PROTOCOL.md). Decide: give bakeoff its own OSM clip, or make cross-world reference reads an explicit documented rule. Check whether earlier rounds (R-005..R-013) also read southampton-build data before comparing R-014 with them.
